title: Progression coach recommends deload on exercises trained to failure by design
steps: Open Quick Workout, add any accessory exercise whose rir_target is 0 (e.g. Machine Incline Press) with 3+ logged sessions averaging RIR 0.
expected: No deload suggestion for an exercise that is intentionally trained to failure per Science-Unified.md:122 ('0 RIR is the default style and is kept').
actual: Coach card reads 'Machine Incline Press: last 3 sessions averaged RIR 0.0. Deload weight: 242.5.' Confirmed live on fresh October data, not just the prior run's June snapshot.
repro: ios-sim/flows/rir-ux-test.json (goto /quick-workout) — no interaction needed, card renders on load
why: programProgression.js's avgRir<2 deload rule and coachingEngine.js's avgRir<1 deload rule both ignore the exercise's own rir_target (0 for accessories, athlete_profile.py:280/ACCESSORY_RIR_TARGET), so intentional failure training reads as a problem. Root-caused in ui-audit/overnight/critique/cbum-training.md #2 (code-only); this pass confirms it live with current data. Not fixed in this pass — it's a cross-cutting logic change (programProgression.js + coachingEngine.js both need the exercise's rir_target threaded through), scoped as a proposal, not a one-line fix.
disposition: proposal — needs Nolan's call on the replacement progression rule (see cbum-training.md #2 concrete change and nippard-training-nutrition.md N3)

title: No UI control for training-focus / goal_priorities anywhere in the app
steps: Open Profile and look for any control that changes training emphasis (powerlifting vs bodybuilding vs cardio).
expected: Some settable control writes user_profiles.training_phase or goal_priorities, since the engine reads and acts on them (allocator.py:91-99, compute_athlete_state.py:805).
actual: Profile has exactly three sections (Identity, Body & Nutrition, Settings) plus Sign Out. Grep of src/ confirms zero writers for training_phase or muscle_emphasis anywhere in the frontend.
why: Directly answers Nolan's own question ('how do I adjust focus between powerlifting/bodybuilding/cardio') — the answer today is you can't, through the app. This is a missing feature, not a code defect, so it's a proposal, not a fix.
disposition: proposal — needs a new Profile control; see cbum-addendum-2026-10-12.md §2 and nippard-training-nutrition.md N4

title: RIR entry breaks the input pattern weight/reps just established
steps: Add an exercise, open the set-entry sheet, fill weight then reps (digit keypad, Next button in a tall right-side column both times), then advance to RIR.
expected: Consistent interaction pattern and confirm-button position across all three fields of one set.
actual: RIR screen replaces the digit grid with 7 color-coded pills and moves the confirm button from the right-column position to a full-width button at the bottom. A pill tap also commits-and-finishes the set in one tap, unlike weight/reps which require digit-then-explicit-advance.
why: Scope addition from Nolan ('not a fan of how RIR logging currently works'). Live-confirmed tap-for-tap. Upstream cause of iosaud-01 and of coachingEngine.js's coaching system going dormant (gated on real RIR data, coachingEngine.js:10-11,32-37) — friction here has a compounding cost. UI redesign, not a quick fix.
disposition: proposal — see cbum-addendum-2026-10-12.md §3 for concrete redesign options

title: Hypertrophy volume counting does not weight by the spec's own effective-reps formula
steps: Compare Science-Unified.md:226-231's Reps_eff = max(0, 5-RIR) stimulus model against compute_hypertrophy()'s actual set-counting logic.
expected: A set at RIR 5+ (per spec, zero hypertrophic stimulus) should not count the same as a set at RIR 0 toward weekly muscle volume.
actual: compute_hypertrophy() (compute_athlete_state.py:319-369) counts any set with weight or reps logged as one hard set, with no RIR weighting. The effective-reps formula is implemented exactly once in the codebase (log_ingest.py's proximity_fatigue_factor) and feeds only the fatigue-cost model, not the volume/MEV-MAV-MRV bars a user sees.
repro: Code read only — no live UI reproduces this directly since the test clone's athlete_state is empty (see Methodology note in the final report); traced via compute_athlete_state.py:319 and log_ingest.py:32-72.
why: Spec/implementation drift found during the Nippard pass, not previously documented. See nippard-training-nutrition.md N1.
disposition: proposal — needs Nolan's call on whether to formally weight volume by effective reps

title: Mid-session navigation does not lose entered set data
steps: Add Bench Press, log a set (weight 295, reps 8, no RIR picked, tap Done), navigate to Today, navigate back to Train.
expected: No data loss per CLAUDE.md's hard constraint ('a workout must never restart or stop once anything has been logged').
actual: Set persisted correctly; Today and Train both rendered the session normally on return. No crash, no lost data.
why: This is a PASS, logged for completeness per the RUNBOOK's 'verify rejected at least something or explain why all held' convention — not a bug. Only one regression scenario was tested in this pass; this does not clear the broader interrupted-session space (lock/background, offline, reload) the September overnight run's RUNBOOK persona situations cover — those were out of this pass's time budget.
